Issued at 236 PM CDT Wed Oct 21 2026

High pressure center to the north is in control today, keeping 
northeasterly winds gentle this afternoon. As the high pressure 
slides eastward, winds will shift overnight tonight to become 
southeasterly. Mostly clear skies are also in place today and into 
tonight, with just some scattered mid to high clouds expected. 
Strong humidity recovery coupled with the light winds overnight 
create the potential for some fog development early Thursday 
morning. Thus far hi-res model guidance is split on the fog 
potential, with mainly the REFS showing some visibility reductions 
over central South Dakota. However, can't rule out fog over both the 
James River Valley and far northeastern South Dakota/western 
Minnesota either due to lighter winds compared to the rest of the 
forecast area and a favorable direction for upslope flow helping 
with the development. 

On Thursday, the high pressure center in control of the region will 
progress eastward, causing a tightening of the pressure gradient 
behind it. Southerly wind gusts will therefore increase Thursday 
afternoon, reaching up to 25-35 miles per hour by the afternoon. The 
strongest gusts are expected mainly along and west of the Missouri 
River, and may persist into the overnight hours. An upper-level 
ridge overhead will support the continuation of above normal 
temperatures. Highs reaching into the upper 70s to low 80s may 
approach daily record highs. 

A southerly low-level jet will move over eastern South Dakota and 
western Minnesota Friday, bringing about a further increase in winds 
over much of the forecast area. There is a fair degree of agreement 
on the jet topping out around 850mb at 40-50 miles per hour. This 
will result in near-Wind Advisory gusts (45 miles per hour or 
higher) near the surface in the afternoon. High-resolution ensembles 
within range of the event give a roughly 10-30% chance (with 
localized areas up to 40-50%) to see gusts of 45+ miles per hour 
Friday afternoon, so the event remains somewhat marginal at this 
point. The jet will advect warm, moist air into the region, pushing 
850mb temperatures up to 20 degrees Celsius and PWATs to 1.25"+, 
both well above the 90th percentile for this time of year. Naturally 
this will create another day of near-record temperatures at the 
surface (highs in the upper 70s to low 80s) and widespread dew 
points in the 50s. The low-level jet will also be responsible for 
supporting some light rain shower development over northeastern 
South Dakota and western Minnesota Friday morning and afternoon. As 
the jet continues overnight Saturday, there is potential for some 
localized downslope winds over the eastern side of the Prairie 
Coteau reaching upwards of Advisory criteria. 

With strong winds both Thursday and Friday coupled with the abnormal 
heat, elevated fire weather conditions will be in place during those 
afternoons. Thursday, Grassland Fire Danger will reach the High 
category over central and parts of north central South Dakota. 
Coverage of High Grassland Fire Danger will expand to cover the 
entire forecast area Friday afternoon, with some pockets of Very 
High Grassland Fire Danger possible. The high dew points (up into 
the 50s) will keep minimum afternoon humidity to the 40-55 percent 
range both days. 

On Saturday, a cold front is set to move across the forecast area. 
Along the boundary, additional rain showers are expected. Behind the 
cold front, there is high confidence in a significant temperature 
drop into the start of next week. While there's naturally still a 
bit of uncertainty, highs are set to be in the upper 40s to low 50s, 
about 5-10 degrees below normal for this time of year. An upper-
level low will track northeast into the region next week, 
potentially bringing additional precipitation chances during the 
early week. An early look at soundings does show some potential for 
saturation in the DGZ and a sub-freezing profile down to the near-
surface layer during the overnight hours, so some of the area may 
potentially see the first flakes of the season.
